title: Personal Loans Late Fees When a FlexLine Fell Behind in the Same or Previous Cycle
content:
## Rule

The pay-cycle form applies only to a Personal Loans loan on fee schedule A or B; a loan on schedule C takes no pay-cycle form, and its late-fee figure is its flat amount, 10.00 USD, whatever the borrower's FlexLine shows. For a loan on schedule A or B the form looks at the borrower's latest FlexLine late fee (on a tie of dates, the first one recorded) and the amount past due on the borrower's open FlexLine (active, frozen or in repayment; a borrower holds at most one), both read from the borrower's FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit records:

1. when that FlexLine late fee was charged for a FlexLine due date no more than 15 days before or after the installment's due date (a count of days between two dates being the later date minus the earlier) and the open FlexLine still has an amount past due, the loan's own late fee is cut to the loan's part of the two amounts past due in that cycle (the FlexLine late fee itself is left as it stands), so the late-fee figure is the schedule figure times the unpaid portion divided by the unpaid portion plus the FlexLine's amount past due;
2. when that FlexLine late fee was instead charged for a FlexLine due date more than 15 but no more than 45 days from the installment's due date, the loan's late fee is held so that it and that FlexLine late fee together stay within the maximum of the loan's own schedule, so the late-fee figure is the schedule figure or the loan's schedule maximum (30.00 USD on schedule A, 15.00 USD on schedule B) less that FlexLine late fee, whichever is smaller, never below zero; a late fee of 0.00 is not charged;
3. in every other case the FlexLine does not change the late-fee figure.

That FlexLine late fee is taken net of every FlexLine fee waiver applied to it: one waived in full counts as no FlexLine late fee, and one waived in part counts at its unwaived amount.

The schedule figure is the schedule's percent of the unpaid portion within the schedule's minimum and maximum, unrounded; the late-fee figure the form sets is the one the late fee is then taken from, held to no more than the unpaid portion and rounded to the cent once, at the end.

## Decision table (schedule A or B loan)

| Days between the FlexLine late fee's due date and the installment's due date | Open FlexLine has an amount past due | Late-fee figure |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 15 | yes | schedule figure times unpaid portion over unpaid portion plus FlexLine amount past due |
| 0 to 15 | no | not changed |
| 16 to 45 | any | smaller of the schedule figure and the schedule maximum less the FlexLine late fee, not below zero |
| above 45, or no FlexLine late fee, or one waived in full | any | not changed |

## Cases (hypothetical schedule A loan, unpaid portion 500.00, schedule figure 25.00)

- FlexLine late fee for a FlexLine due date 4 days after the installment's, open FlexLine 300.00 past due: 25.00 times 500.00 over 800.00 is 15.625.
- FlexLine late fee of 20.00 for a due date 30 days earlier: the smaller of 25.00 and 30.00 less 20.00, so 10.00.
- The same 20.00 FlexLine late fee with 8.00 of it waived: counted at 12.00, the smaller of 25.00 and 18.00, so 18.00.
- FlexLine late fee 30.00 for a due date 20 days earlier: 30.00 less 30.00 is 0.00, and no late fee is charged.
